gen-dafont-franchise-gf-hanuman: Tall, tight, and stern. Franchise packs its letters shoulder to shoulder, while Hanuman, a classic serif with a high waist, spreads its s terminals wide and lets the page loosen up. Make the heading a good deal larger than the text.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-kadwa: Dignified and strong, Franchise stands up tall with its letters crowded close, built for announcing. Kadwa, a serif with open-ended curves and a generous x-height, is the one built for carrying the actual sentences.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noticia-text: Narrow, tall lowercase crammed tight together gives Franchise its look, every stroke drawn like neon tube. And Noticia Text, a serif with big entrance strokes into its curves, fills out the lines beneath with a literary warmth.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-piazzolla: Franchise stands tall and clean, its letters jammed against each other with the c tips pulled well apart. But Piazzolla, a text serif whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, sprawls out underneath with a pried-open e and an authoritative hush.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-pridi: Lean, upright, and unfussy up top. Pridi, a text serif with almost capital-sized small letters and generous gaps where curves meet stems, makes a long passage feel spacious and settled beneath Franchise.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-scope-one: Scope One is a text serif whose counters spill outward, with stubby ascenders and descenders beside a big x-height, under Franchise's wire-thin lettering. Long stretches of it read generously.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-slabo-13px: Bookish and dignified, Slabo 13px sits below a marker-tip Franchise. Slabo 13px is a serif with large open counters, so if the body gets blown up very large, those openings start to gape.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-suwannaphum: An o with sides and top equally thick marks Franchise out, tall and tightly packed. Suwannaphum, a serif with a paperclip-open c and a high woodblock-like x-height, makes a long passage feel dignified and editorial.
gen-dafont-franchise-switzer: Narrow, upright, and tightly packed. Franchise crowds its tall lowercase together, and Switzer, a sans with wire-like letterforms and c tips that never creep toward touching, gives the pair an approachable Swiss openness below.
gen-dafont-galaxy-gf-domine: Domine is a classic serif with compact ascenders and tall lowercase. Galaxy leads with neon-glass tubes of uninterrupted stroke, loose and cosmic, while Domine texts hold their light strokes close and steady.
